question: What is the main goal of nursing care during normal female life changes?

options.C: Distinguishing normal variations from health issues
options.D: Treating every life stage as a disease

explanation: Nurses must recognize standard body shifts to offer reassurance and avoid treating healthy processes as diseases. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand normal female reproductive milestones?

options.A: To support holistic care respecting individual differences
options.B: To stop natural hormone decline in older age
options.C: To make sure every woman gets medical synchronization
options.D: To set the exact age of first menstruation globally

explanation: Knowing standard development helps nurses give personalized support that respects personal and cultural differences. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which gland directly releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to stimulate the pituitary?
explanation: The hypothalamus is the part of the brain that releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone in pulses. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h2)

question: How do ovarian hormones regulate the upper structures of the reproductive hormone axis?

options.A: By bypassing the brain to control uterine lining thickness
options.B: By using negative or positive feedback loops
options.C: By turning directly into gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: By permanently stopping pituitary hormone output

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone send feedback to the hypothalamus and pituitary to control hormone release. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers the release of a mature egg during the menstrual cycle?
explanation: A sharp peak in luteinizing hormone in the middle of the cycle is what triggers ovulation. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which hormone mainly causes the secretory changes in the uterine lining during the second half of the cycle?
explanation: Progesterone from the corpus luteum changes the uterine lining to get it ready for a fertilized egg to attach. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the earliest outward physical sign of female puberty called?
explanation: Breast development, known as thelarche, is usually the first visible sign of puberty in young females. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do many young girls have irregular periods right after their first menstrual period?

options.A: Adrenal glands temporarily stop making hormones
options.B: The uterus lacks receptors for circulating estrogen
options.C: Permanent scarring stops normal monthly bleeding
options.D: The hormone control axis is still immature

explanation: An immature feedback loop often leads to cycles without ovulation, causing irregular bleeding in early adolescence. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h4)

question: In which specific part of the reproductive tract does fertilization normally happen?
explanation: The ampulla of the fallopian tube provides the right spot for the sperm and egg to meet. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h5)

question: What factor creates a fertile window that lasts for several days before ovulation?

options.A: Sperm can survive inside the female reproductive tract for multiple days
options.B: Unfertilized eggs stay alive in the uterus for a week
options.C: Cervical mucus blocks germs but traps healthy eggs
options.D: Progesterone triggers the quick release of stored eggs

explanation: Because sperm can live for up to five days inside the body, having sex before ovulation can still lead to pregnancy. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h5)

question: How many months in a row without a period are needed to confirm menopause?
explanation: Menopause is officially diagnosed when a full year passes without any natural menstrual bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h6)

question: What primary body change causes the high follicle-stimulating hormone levels seen in perimenopause?

options.A: Overproduction of hormones by the posterior pituitary gland
options.B: Complete stop of hypothalamic releasing hormones
options.C: Fewer ovarian follicles and lower inhibin production
options.D: Direct stimulation of the pituitary by aged adrenal tissues

explanation: Fewer follicles mean less inhibin is made, which removes the feedback brake and causes follicle-stimulating hormone levels to climb. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT normally checked during a basic menstrual history assessment?
explanation: While bone health is important for older women, a standard menstrual history focuses on cycle length, duration, and flow rather than bone injuries. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is a non-judgmental environment important when taking a reproductive health history?

options.A: It stops the patient from asking about birth control
options.B: It helps the patient share sensitive and accurate health details
options.C: It immediately stops any hormone changes
options.D: It legally removes the need for a physical exam

explanation: Patients are more likely to share honest details about private reproductive health matters when they feel safe and respected. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main aim of promotive nursing care for normal female body processes?

options.B: Empowering women with knowledge to manage their reproductive health
options.C: Stopping natural hormone changes to remove period symptoms
options.D: Making every woman use hormonal birth control

explanation: Promotive care aims to educate women so they can understand and manage their normal body processes with confidence. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h8)

question: A young girl is worried because her cycle length changes by a few days each month. What is the best first nursing response?

options.A: Explain that slight cycle changes can be normal in the teenage years
options.B: Tell her to start daily birth control pills to force exact regularity
options.C: Refer her right away to a hormone specialist
options.D: Warn her that this means her reproductive system is failing

explanation: Reassuring teenagers with clear facts about how the body develops helps reduce worry about normal early cycle changes. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h8)
